You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook and recommended pushbacks
**Status of source material:** Seller's draft and Disclosure Letter reviewed as the counterparty's untrusted proposal, tested against our playbook. Nothing in the Seller's package changes our authorised positions.

---

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Almost every limitation-of-liability term moves materially against us, and several structural proposals (collapsing Title into the general regime, applying all limitations "to all Claims of any nature", blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, whole-data-room disclosure) would, in combination, hollow out the Warranty package. Separately, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update — it concedes that Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment and the bonus funding are all unresolved. We should use the Disclosure Letter's own admissions against the Seller Update's "addressed/adequate/settled" characterisations.

Critically: **no fallback authority has been given by Amelia Frost on any item.** We hold at 25% / AUD 6,000,000 and 24 months.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 General Warranty cap — Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 opening; 20% is a conditional fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — none given.
**Analysis:** The Seller has landed directly on our fallback number. Whether that is coincidence or a leak of our range, we cannot concede it in this round. Reverting to 25% also preserves negotiating headroom for a later trade (e.g. cap vs basket vs period).
**Pushback:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal 20% is available.

### 2.2 Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar once exceeded.
**Analysis:** Three independent departures, each worse for us: (i) de minimis is 5x ours; (ii) basket is 5x ours; (iii) the "excess only" structure converts the basket from a tipping basket into a deductible, so AUD 250,000 of valid loss is simply lost. On a AUD 24m price the Seller's basket is >1% — well above market for a deal this size. Note also the interaction with the de minimis: a cluster of AUD 20,000 claims (e.g. several Sandbar-type items or on-cost miscalculations) would never count toward the basket at all.
**Pushback:** Revert all three. If forced to trade, the tipping-vs-deductible point is the most valuable to hold; it is also the one the Seller buried in a subordinate clause.

### 2.3 Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general claims; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
**Analysis:** Two problems. The 18 months is again our undisclosed fallback. More dangerous is the second sentence: it is a default rule that makes every limitation (cap, basket, time, knowledge bar) apply to Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims unless we have *expressly* carved each one out. This is a hidden general-regime override and conflicts directly with our "keep categories separate" principle. Drafting burden flips to us and any omission is fatal.
**Pushback:** 24 months. Delete the default-application sentence and replace with the reverse: limitations in clause 12 apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated; Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, fraud and covenant claims are governed solely by their own regimes.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title — same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity"
**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and 18-month period.
**Playbook:** separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** This is the single most serious departure. If the Seller does not actually own the shares (or they are encumbered), we would be limited to AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase and barred after 18 months. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason — a separate schedule is trivially simple. Combined with 2.3's default rule and 2.6's knowledge exclusion ("discoverable from public records"), a title defect appearing on a register search we could have run would be irrecoverable.
**Pushback:** Reject outright. Insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime: cap = purchase price; period = 6 years minimum (consider 7 for consistency with the longest statutory limitation we could face); no basket/de minimis; no knowledge or disclosure qualification.

### 2.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" — Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; no one may waive this.
**Analysis:** There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller Update. "All Claims of any nature" on its face purports to cap and time-bar a fraud claim and to use non-reliance to defeat a misrepresentation claim. A court would likely refuse to enforce a limitation of liability for the Seller's own fraud, but we should not rely on that — the clause invites litigation over enforceability and would operate fully against negligent or reckless misstatement. This is a non-negotiable item under the playbook.
**Pushback:** Insert express, non-waivable carve-out: nothing in clauses 8, 9, 12, 13 or 20 limits or excludes liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or anyone on their behalf, to the maximum extent permitted by law. Confirm the ACL-style statutory remedies are not excluded where exclusion would be unenforceable in any event.

### 2.6 Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records".
**Playbook:** delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Analysis:** This is an actual-and-constructive-knowledge bar extending to our advisers and to anything theoretically "discoverable". Read with Schedule 7's whole-data-room disclosure (2.7), it means: everything in the data room is disclosed, everything discoverable is known, and the Buyer therefore has no warranty claim for any matter touched on anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012 — which is every live issue on this deal (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the incident, Sandbar). The clause also runs the wrong way: warranties are a risk-allocation mechanism, and the point of a warranty is that the Seller bears the risk even for matters the Buyer might have found. The only legitimate knowledge concept in an SPA is *Seller* knowledge qualifying particular warranties.
**Pushback:** Delete clause 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on something, offer at most: no claim for matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter (per 2.7). Any Seller-knowledge qualifier must reference named individuals (propose the Harbourglass directors and Paperbark's CEO/CFO) after due and careful enquiry.

### 2.7 Disclosure — Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** general disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at 22 Sept 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
**Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** The data room dump is the standard seller attempt to convert diligence into disclosure. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is undefined and open-ended — it could be read to include ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court lists, land titles. Para 1.4 ("nothing admits breach, liability, materiality… or that any consent… is legally required") sits uncomfortably with disclosure's purpose: the Seller wants the protective effect of disclosure while disclaiming that anything disclosed matters. Note the Disclosure Letter itself is dated to the data room cut-off; anything added after 22 September is not covered, and we should hold the Seller to that.
**Pushback:** Disclosure is effective only if made in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed ("fair disclosure" standard). Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures; the data room may be referenced only where a specific paragraph points to a specific document for a specific matter. Delete "publicly searchable corporate records". Para 1.4 can stay only if expressly without prejudice to the fair-disclosure test.

### 2.8 Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3
**Seller:** "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent.
**Disclosure Letter para 2:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30% of revenue); consent clause 11.2 with conditions at 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied.**
**Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~30% of revenue; losing it would materially impair the business we are paying AUD 24m for. "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" means a conditional consent (e.g. consent subject to price concessions, a guarantee, or a step-in right) would satisfy the CP even if the 11.3 conditions are never met and Bluefen later terminates. The Seller Update's "addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.
**Pushback:** CP requires (a) Bluefen's unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 in a form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, and (b) written evidence that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen, both before Completion. Seller obligation lifted to all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours with a Buyer right of participation in the Bluefen discussions. Add a specific warranty that Bluefen has not indicated an intention to terminate, reduce volume or renegotiate. Consider a price adjustment or retention if the consent carries commercial conditions.

### 2.9 Riverlark facility — Clause 2 / 7
**Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter para 3:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2; **not repaid, no final discharge included.**
**Playbook:** current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. Completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt in the target and no release means (i) the change-of-control at cl 8.1 may trigger an event of default on Completion, (ii) the bank's security over the Company's assets (and potentially the shares) remains, so we acquire encumbered shares/assets, and (iii) we depend on the Seller performing after it has been paid. There is no mention of a payout figure in the funds flow.
**Pushback:** Require: a payout letter from Riverlark dated no earlier than two business days before Completion; repayment direct to Riverlark out of the purchase price at Completion (netting from the Seller's proceeds); executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR releases delivered at Completion; Riverlark's written waiver of cl 8.1. Any slippage to post-Completion release needs an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking in escrow plus Amelia Frost sign-off — flag that this is *not* currently approved.

### 2.10 Funds flow and employee bonuses — DD-005
**Seller:** bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised; funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics".
**Disclosure Letter para 5:** AUD 420,000 conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.**
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion — our act — and are payable by the Company (the entity we will own). Unless itemised, the Company pays them post-Completion out of our economics, together with superannuation guarantee and NSW payroll tax on the gross amount. The Seller's phrase "a matter for the Seller" is only reassuring if it is translated into a mechanism; currently it is not.
**Pushback:** Add line item: AUD 420,000 plus all superannuation, payroll tax, PAYG withholding and other on-costs, either (a) deducted from the purchase price as a Debt-like item, or (b) paid by the Seller into the Company immediately before Completion. Seller warranty that DD-005 is a complete list of transaction-triggered payments. Clarify whether continued-employment conditions mean any amount is deferred — if so, the deferred amount must also be funded.

### 2.11 Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1
**Seller:** indemnity limited to SOW3 payment, "adequate".
**Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 transfers SOW3 Project Materials only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not independent verification; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Playbook:** broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 — it is that IP we are paying for (SOW3 Project Materials) may still legally sit with Ironquay. A payment-only indemnity does not cover: loss of the materials, Ironquay refusing to assign even after payment, third-party claims, re-development cost, or infringement exposure if the Company keeps using unassigned materials. We also do not actually know whether the fee is unpaid — DD-010 is the Company's own ledger.
**Pushback:** (i) CP or Completion deliverable: Ironquay receipt/confirmation that all SOW3 fees are cleared and an executed confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials. (ii) Broaden cl 11.1 to an indemnity for all Loss arising from any defect in or failure to obtain title to the Ironquay materials, any Ironquay claim, and any cost of re-procuring equivalent materials — outside the general cap/basket. (iii) Keep the cure: if the Seller procures cleared payment plus assignment before Completion, the indemnity narrows to residual claims. (iv) Request Ironquay's own statement of account.

### 2.12 Export/privacy incident — DD-006
**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter para 6:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary; not characterised as a breach; no loss amount.
**Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Analysis:** We should neither accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation nor overstate it. What matters is that the facts are not yet known and the Seller is trying to close before they are. Data of this kind is likely personal information under the Privacy Act; whether it triggers the notifiable data breach scheme depends on access and likely serious harm — which the Seller admits it has not determined. The risk to us is inheriting an unassessed regulatory and customer-relations issue.
**Pushback:** (i) Covenant: preserve all logs, link-access records and correspondence; complete a documented investigation (ideally with external forensic support) before Completion; provide the Buyer with the report and all updates. (ii) Warranty that the investigation and any required notifications have been completed as at Completion, with a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification cost, customer claims) outside the general basket, cap to be discussed. (iii) Do not accept any Disclosure Letter language that treats the incident as fairly disclosed in its entirety — the disclosure is expressly incomplete. (iv) Internally: we make no assumption of breach, harm or notification duty, and attach no number to this.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals — DD-008 / DD-011
**Seller:** ordinary-course operating costs.
**Disclosure Letter para 8:** three related renewals, AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 aggregate; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** Agree with the playbook — not every supplier commitment is Debt. But the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure, and the fact the three are "related" and must be "read together for timing/scope" suggests they may be a single AUD 330,000 commitment split to appear routine. Key questions: were they entered or renewed between signing of the LOI and Completion? Are they terminable without penalty? Do they relate to the ongoing business or to run-off? Has any amount accrued but not been paid in the Accounts?
**Pushback:** Request the three agreements and renewal correspondence; confirm whether any pre-Completion period cost is unpaid. Pending that, treat as neutral — no price deduction demand, but reserve position in the Working Capital / Debt definitions and add to the ordinary-course conduct covenant that no further renewals occur without Buyer consent.

### 2.14 Tax and IP — "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** tax and IP warranties fold into the 20% cap / 18 months / basket.
**Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate categories; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
**Analysis:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller is attempting to deem settlement by assertion. Tax in particular is conventionally subject to a longer period (tied to the Commissioner's amendment periods) and often a higher cap or standalone tax indemnity; IP interacts directly with the Ironquay issue. We should not counter with specific numbers in this round absent instructions — simply reject the deeming.
**Pushback:** State in the mark-up that Tax and IP warranties and any tax indemnity are reserved for separate negotiation and are not subject to clause 12 unless and until expressly agreed. Do not propose a figure.

### 2.15 Title — DD-012 share register
**Seller:** title evidenced by the Company share register.
**Disclosure Letter para 10:** register records Harbourglass as 100% holder; this is the source relied on; Buyer has not completed own verification.
**Playbook:** independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** A share register is maintained by the Company — i.e. by the Seller's appointees. It is prima facie evidence, not conclusive, and it says nothing about charges over the shares (Riverlark may well hold share security — see 2.9), options, pre-emption rights or the Seller's own authority to sell. The Seller's own para 10 concedes it is merely "the source relied on".
**Pushback:** Obtain independently: ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass for security over the shares; the Company constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption/consent rights); Harbourglass board minutes and, if required, shareholder approval authorising the sale; director/secretary certificates at Completion. Title warranties remain Fundamental per 2.4 and unqualified by DD-012 or any knowledge bar.

### 2.16 Secondary items from the Disclosure Letter
- **Office lease (para 7 / DD-007):** notification obligation only, not landlord consent. Accept, but require the notification to be given pre-Completion with a copy to us, and warranty that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (para 9 / DD-009):** assignment restriction; share sale not stated to trigger consent. Reasonable, but ask for the actual clause to confirm there is no change-of-control limb, and add to the no-consents warranty.
- **Para 11 reservation:** Confirms the Seller is not representing any conclusion — which cuts both ways. It reinforces that the "addressed / adequate / settled / not material" statements in the Seller Update are advocacy, not disclosure.

---

## 3. How the Seller's provisions interact (why the package is worse than its parts)

Taken individually, each Seller term is aggressive. Taken together they form a closed loop:

1. **Whole-data-room disclosure (Sch 7)** → every live issue is "disclosed".
2. **Constructive knowledge bar (cl 8.3)** → every disclosed/discoverable matter is "known" and therefore unclaimable.
3. **Default application of limitations to all Claims (cl 13)** + **Title in the general regime** → even Title, Tax, IP and indemnity claims are capped at AUD 4.8m, deductible-basketed and 18-month limited.
4. **No fraud carve-out, all limitations apply to "Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** → the non-reliance clause and exclusive-remedy clause close off the misrepresentation route.

The result is that a buyer paying AUD 24m could be left without any effective remedy for the very matters identified in diligence. Our mark-up should be framed around dismantling this loop, not just adjusting the numbers.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Item | Seller position | Our mark-up | Priority |
|---|------|-----------------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; no fallback authorised | High |
| 2 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k, deductible | 5k / 50k, tipping (first dollar) | High |
| 3 | General claims period | 18 months | 24 months; no fallback authorised | High |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" default | Insert | Delete; reverse the default | Critical |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | In general regime | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 yrs, no basket/knowledge | Critical |
| 6 | Fraud / wilful concealment | No carve-out; "all Claims of any nature" | Express non-waivable carve-out from every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance | Critical |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge cl 8.3 | Blanket, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Delete; Seller-knowledge qualifiers only, named persons + reasonable enquiry | Critical |
| 8 | Disclosure Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2 | Whole data room + public records | Specific fair disclosure only; delete general disclosures | Critical |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion | Critical |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion; post-Completion only with irrevocable undertaking + A. Frost approval | Critical |
| 11 | Bonuses DD-005 | Not itemised | AUD 420k + super/payroll tax/on-costs as line item or Seller-funded; completeness warranty | High |
| 12 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Receipt + confirmatory assignment at Completion; broadened IP indemnity preserving SOW3 cure; independent Ironquay statement | High |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Log preservation, completed investigation and updates pre-Completion; specific indemnity; no assumption of breach or quantum | Medium–High |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Request documents; assess; no automatic Debt treatment; add to conduct covenant | Medium |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | Reserved; expressly outside cl 12 pending separate agreement | High |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/constitution/authority evidence; register not conclusive | High |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | Accept subject to sight of clauses and no-consents warranty | Low |

**Process points**
- Respond with a full mark-up rather than an issues list, so the Seller cannot treat silence on any clause as acceptance — particularly given its "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" drafting.
- Do not reference 20% or 18 months anywhere in the mark-up or cover note. If the Seller asks whether those are achievable, the answer is that no such authority exists.
- Send the open-items list (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 investigation, bonus funding, title searches) as Completion deliverables / CPs rather than leaving them to warranties — the Disclosure Letter confirms all five are presently unsatisfied.
- Escalate to Amelia Frost only if and when the Seller refuses the 25% / 24-month position in a later round; nothing in this round requires her approval because we are conceding nothing.
=== END ADVICE ===
